extracted.intended_audience: Researchers invited to review manuscripts for Frontiers in Public Health (journal peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for researchers acting as peer reviewers for Frontiers in Public Health, describing the single-anonymized collaborative review model, pre-acceptance considerations (expertise, time, conflicts), how to write the review, interactive review participation, and post-review recognition/confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model: single-anonymized
rubrics_metrics.description: Frontiers operates a single-anonymized model during the review process: the reviewers know who the authors are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers know authors to offer a full assessment in context and to ensure they can avoid any potential competing interests in accepting a review invitation. Frontiers discloses the name of all endorsing reviewers upon publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative peer review platform
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review platform is collaborative: it unites authors, reviewers, and the handling editor in a direct online dialog, enabling quick iterations and facilitating consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and reviewers work with the authors to improve their manuscript; the platform allows direct interaction, viewing of responses, and commentary on others' reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review phase: use the review questionnaire
rubrics_metrics.description: During the first review phase reviewers assess the paper independently from each other and the authors and complete a review questionnaire tailored for each article type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access and review the manuscript and supporting documents in the online forum; when submitting the review report, also submit a recommendation to the editor. Reviewers may directly endorse the manuscript and finalize their review if it meets acceptance criteria. Handling editor reviews reports before activating interactive review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive review phase: engage with authors and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Once interactive review is activated, authors can view and respond to reviewers' comments and reviewers are notified when the author has replied or resubmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers can enter a dialog with the author to request clarifications or further revisions, access and comment on other reviewers' reports, endorse the paper if changes are adequate, or recommend rejection if the paper cannot be brought up to standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expertise match (Is the manuscript within my expertise?)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the manuscript is suitably within your area of expertise before accepting the invitation to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not within your expertise, decline the invite and consider suggesting alternative relevant experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time availability / timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether you have the time to complete the review; reviewers are requested to complete their reports within 7 days after accepting the invite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to review invitations as soon as possible. If seven days is insufficient, or there will be a delay after accepting, contact the editorial office to request an extension or arrange another time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: After accepting, reviewers are asked to complete a short questionnaire regarding conflicts of interest to establish any relationship with the author(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose all answers in full: conflicts are assessed case-by-case and may not be disqualifying. Full disclosure allows the editor to judge suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on the quality of the science objectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers' aims should be to focus on the quality of the science objectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assess the author; focus solely on the research itself. It is not necessary to flag small copy-editing errors (the production team will fix those).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the manuscript's stated scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the focus on what the manuscript is aiming to do, as explained in the authors' 'contribution to the field' statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid recommending that authors vastly expand the scope of the manuscript or take them outside their manuscript's intended scope (e.g. telling them to address unrelated topics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should seek to recommend reasonable improvements in a polite and impersonal tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show professional courtesy by thinking about what you would want to receive on a paper of your own. Explain why something is good as well as why it needs change, and recommend concrete, reasonable improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider field-specific elements
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are elements of the research specific to your field, apply your expertise to give feedback on these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field-specific comments are helpful to all involved in the manuscript's review process; point out domain-relevant methodological or interpretive issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be thorough and avoid vague/brief reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors find precise and detailed feedback extremely helpful; brief reports often lead to additional questions from authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure recommendations and decisions are explained clearly. Use the detailed questionnaire provided in the collaborative review platform to provide a clear assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include key points and a clear recommendation in the initial report
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial report should be thorough and provide all the necessary feedback upfront.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While later revisions may bring up new questions, ensure you include your key points in your initial report and conclude with a clear recommendation for the handling editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain engagement and do not drop out
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure an efficient process, reviewers should try to submit responses on time and remain engaged through the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need an extension or must withdraw, request this in the review forum or contact the editorial office. Keep lines of communication open; place yourself in the authors' position awaiting feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and platform assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: If you encounter issues during review or need assistance using the review platform, you should contact the journal office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the journal for any concerns with the manuscript, platform help, or to request deadline changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition, confidentiality and handling of reviewer reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers who endorse a manuscript for publication are recognized by being named on the published article; those who recommend rejection or withdraw are not named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a report is submitted, reviewers receive a confirmation email including a copy of their report which may be used to obtain recognition. The report itself is not to be shared in any public forum; reports are retained by the journal even if a reviewer recommends rejection or withdraws.
